source.title: Relative Representations for Cognitive Graphs
source.authors: Alex B. Kiefer; C. L. Buckley

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representation mapping with relative representations in discrete cognitive graphs, a new model setting and a post-hoc reconstruction procedure rather than the original continuous-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own cross-agent mapping results, which bear on representational alignment and interchangeability. It also cites results from other work; those are not recorded as rows. It reports that mappings improve when anchors come from the trajectory being reconstructed, but does not give a separate numerical result for that choice.
record.test_reason: Maps one trained CSCG agent's belief messages onto another's via post-hoc relative representations. This tests V4 (mapping across models) in a new setting: discrete graph-structured state-space models rather than neural networks. Not T2: the method and system both differ from the originals. No scale sweep, vision-language pairs, universal features or convergence-measure comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present this as a proof of principle that relative representations apply to posterior distributions over discrete latent spaces. They also present a learning-free method to reconstruct one agent's absolute beliefs from another's. Recovery is above chance in all conditions and near-perfect when messages are conditioned on actions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses relative representations and cross-model similarity, but extends them to discrete CSCG message distributions and reconstructs the target model's absolute messages post hoc with a softmax-weighted anchor combination; the paper notes this avoids requiring a relative-representation layer during training.
record.method_sensitivity: More anchors improve reconstruction; cosine performs slightly better than negative Jensen-Shannon distance; anchors sampled from the trajectory being reconstructed improve accuracy relative to uniformly sampled random-walk anchors; conditioning messages on actions as well as observations substantially increases accuracy; mapping outcomes differ by room relationship and mapping direction.

fits_no_version.finding: CSCG agents trained from different random initializations and random walks on the same room learn cognitive maps whose forward messages are identical up to a permutation of clone units. A permutation mapping recovers beliefs in 84% of cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: V3 analog for discrete latent-state (HMM) models: the same structure is learned across seeds, but in different unit bases.

record.problems: The experiments use toy CSCG rooms and are described as preliminary. The main table covers the challenging observation-only setting and reports means and SDs over 100 trials; the action-conditioned result is only summarized in prose. Several mapping conditions remain incomplete, and the paper says broader comparisons with alternative alignment methods remain to be assessed.
record.rows_left_out: No reported numerical results bearing on the claim were left out. The text says trajectory-sampled anchors improve mapping but gives no separate value for that comparison.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no differing architectures, objectives or data.
No vision or language models or paired data.
No neural networks. The CSCG permutation analog is recorded under fits_no_version.
No linear maps, layer stitching or unpaired mapping; no neural models.
No comparison of convergence/similarity measures as measures of alignment; no out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of plateau or of what causes alignment. Room dissimilarity is an imposed design, not a measured alignment ceiling.

missing.what: Mapping is more accurate with anchors sampled from the trajectory being reconstructed; no value is given.
Action-conditioned results per condition (e.g. near-perfect isomorphic mapping) are stated only in prose.
The permutation mapping fails for high-uncertainty states and degrades when the learned map does not converge to the true topology.

record.verdict_notes: Toy 6x8 rooms. The system is CSCGs (clone-structured HMMs), not neural networks, so links to versions naming networks were dropped. V6 and V7 links were removed because anchor/metric effects concern mapping quality, not a convergence measure, and imposed room dissimilarity is not an alignment ceiling. Tranche changed from T2 to T3. The record's V6 label also cited r21, a row not linked to V6.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no comparison of independently trained neural networks with differing architectures, objectives, or data.
No vision-language models, paired images and captions, or scale/performance comparison.
Tests CSCG agents with distinct random initializations and observation sequences, not neural-network features or shared subspaces across general neural architectures.

Tests message reconstruction across CSCG agents using a post-hoc relative-representation mapping; does not test layer stitching, relative representations trained as model layers, or unpaired-data mapping.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Tests cosine versus negative Jensen-Shannon distance, anchor count, and message/room conditions; does not provide a broad sweep of similarity measures or out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports incomplete mappings across several room conditions, but does not test scale-related plateaus or establish whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain alignment.

relationships.condition: CSCG agents on identical rooms or the large-to-small expansion, observation-only messages; and all settings with action-conditioned messages
relationships.reason: RR recovery is 89–97% with cosine 0.98–0.99 (r9, r10, r13, r14); the text reports >99% in most settings with actions (r21).
relationships.display_finding: Observation-only recovery reached 89–97% with cosine 0.98–0.99, while action-conditioned messages exceeded 99% recovery in most settings.

relationships.condition: Observation-only messages across partially dissimilar rooms (isomorphic, small-to-large, shifted, landmark)
relationships.reason: Recovery is only 34–47% with cosine 0.52–0.67, though well above the ~2% chance level (r11, r12, r15–r20).
relationships.display_finding: Message recovery reached 34–47% with cosine 0.52–0.67, exceeding approximately 2% chance recovery but remaining incomplete.

relationships.condition: Choice of anchor count and similarity function in the RR reconstruction
relationships.reason: Mapping quality rises with anchor count (r22, figure only) and drops slightly with Jensen-Shannon instead of cosine (r23).
relationships.display_finding: Mapping quality improved with more anchors and decreased slightly when Jensen–Shannon replaced cosine similarity.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CSCG agents trained to convergence on the same room with distinct random walks and initializations
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports messages identical up to a permutation and strong mapping results in the identical-room condition (r3-r4, r9-r10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Relative-representation mappings for identical rooms, large-to-small expansion, and action-conditioned messages
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is high in identical and large-to-small conditions, cosine similarity is near 1 in those conditions, and the authors report greater than 99% accuracy in most settings when actions are included (r9-r10, r13-r14, r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Observation-only mappings for isomorphic, small-to-large, shifted, and landmark room conditions
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is incomplete and varies substantially across room relationships; several conditions have modest recovery or cosine similarity (r11-r12, r15-r20).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Anchor count, similarity metric, and message-conditioning choices tested in the reported CSCG experiments
reader_labels.reason: The authors report improved reconstruction with more anchors, a slight performance decline when replacing cosine with negative Jensen-Shannon distance, and much higher accuracy when conditioning messages on actions as well as observations (r21-r23).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Observation-only mapping across the reported room conditions
reader_labels.reason: The cross-agent mapping is often incomplete, especially across partially dissimilar rooms, while still recovering beliefs above chance as described by the authors (r11-r12, r15-r20).
